rationale: The cap is 60 percent of CPI per year for sitting tenants. Over several years any real rise in market rents makes it bind for long tenancies; at enactment, after the early-1990s slowdown, how soon it binds is less certain.
evidence: For a covered unit, the landlord may raise the rent of a sitting tenant once a year by no more than the allowable increase, which is 60 percent of the rise in the regional consumer price index.

rationale: An existing Rent Board with refund powers and just-cause eviction rules; tenants have a strong incentive to petition.
evidence: The Rent Board, operating since 1979, hears petitions and orders refunds (policy text).

rationale: Small buildings can be sold to owner-occupiers, converted to shared ownership or redeveloped; the record does not say how hard conversion is.
The limit protects the sitting tenant; on a voluntary move the rent resets, so the benefit is lost on leaving and cannot be sold.
evidence: When a tenant leaves voluntarily, the landlord may set the rent for the next tenant freely, after which the limit applies again.

rationale: Uncovered units (newer buildings, vacated units at reset rents) are in the same city and serve the same tenant pool.
